label: URL
help: The page to capture. Captured at export time in a real browser engine.

label: Scroll depth
help: How far down the page to scroll before capturing. 0 = top, 1 = bottom. For a video, this is where the pan starts.

label: Scroll to (video)
help: Video export only: pan down to this depth over the clip - a scroll of the page from 'Scroll depth' to here. Set it equal to 'Scroll depth' for a still hold. Ignored for image formats.

label: Zoom
help: Browser zoom level - magnifies the page before the shot (like Ctrl/Cmd +), so even a bitmap capture is enlarged and crisp rather than upscaled. 1 = 100%.

label: Settle delay (ms)
help: Time to wait after load (and after scrolling) before the shot - lets fonts, images and animations settle.

label: Custom CSS
help: CSS injected into the page before the screenshot - e.g. hide a cookie banner (.cookie-bar { display: none }) or restyle elements.

label: Top
help: Trim in from the top edge, as a 0–0.9 fraction of the height. Raster (png/jpg/svg) only.

label: Right
help: Trim in from the right edge, as a 0–0.9 fraction of the width.

label: Bottom
help: Trim in from the bottom edge, as a 0–0.9 fraction of the height.

label: Left
help: Trim in from the left edge, as a 0–0.9 fraction of the width.

label: Recolour
help: Recolour the whole page before capture. 'Hue shift' rotates every colour by the angle below; 'Tint' desaturates then washes it in the tint colour.

label: Hue angle
help: Degrees to rotate every colour by when Recolour is 'Hue shift'.

label: Tint colour
help: The colour the page is washed in when Recolour is 'Tint'.

label: Compare viewports

options.label: Desktop and phone, side by side

help: Capture the same page twice - once at the export size, once at the phone viewport below - and lay both out in one frame. Still formats only; a webm/mp4 scroll pan stays a single desktop frame.

label: Phone width
help: Viewport width for the second capture, in px. 390 is a current iPhone / Pixel class device.

label: Phone height
help: Viewport height for the second capture, in px. It also sets the phone frame's proportions.
